cross_lane_assumptions: Lane 4 composes verbs through execute_action with the payloads in VERBS.md.
Recovery callers must persist and re-supply the exact original Fabric intent payload; the journal binds it by input hash and refuses mismatches.
ExecutorContext.github_api is the read transport for write readback/reconciliation; production must set it together with the write transport when the owner enables the seam.
github.write.reconcile and git.push.reconcile are read-only and deliberately allowed under STOP (loop.reconciliation_capable).
likely_conflicts: src/jarvis_foundry/fabric/loop.py: capability seeds, verifier predicates, reconciliation_capable set (small additions; merge cleanly if other lanes touch nearby lines).
src/jarvis_foundry/fabric/executors.py: git/github handler block and HANDLERS map.
src/jarvis_foundry/v3_git.py: push now has a STARTED crash-window branch; other lanes calling GitEffectAdapter.push see GitReconcilePending instead of a potential re-execution.
src/jarvis_foundry/connectors/git.py: GitConnector.push no-op pre-check calls git status + ls-remote before delegating to v3_git.GitEffectAdapter.
connectors/github_write.py endpoint regex now accepts optional /{number}/comments; collection reconcile paginates (page 1 request shape unchanged).
integration_order_notes: Land connectors/github_write.py + connectors/git.py + v3_git.py first; fabric/executors.py and fabric/loop.py depend on them.
github_write_dispatch_settings is default-off; no behavior change for existing contexts.
Existing github.issue.create / github.pull_request.create semantics are preserved; the executor refactor to github_write_intent produces identical provider payloads.
next_highest_value_work: Real live proof against an owner-provided throwaway GitHub repository (needs explicit owner authorization; do not invent it).
Wire a mission/Executive recovery step that automatically emits github.write.reconcile / git.push.reconcile for FROZEN developer effects discovered in the journal (Lane 4/Executive composition).
Extend github.pull_request.publish recovery when the driver plan is unavailable (currently the caller re-supplies the plan through publish).

Git push reconciliation requires the caller to remember action_id + expected_head; a persisted push intent record (action id + SHA + remote) would let a recovery scan find candidates without caller memory.
Add a Fabric-visible git.remote_state action if Lane 4 needs structured remote facts without pushing (connector API already exists).
